questions.question: A yellow traffic light means the light will soon turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and safely leave the intersection.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and safely leave the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, you should exit the intersection as quickly and safely as possible.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They get shorter as speed increases.
They do not change with speed.
They get longer as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They get longer as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds create longer stopping distances and more severe crashes. As speed increases, the chance of serious injury or death also increases. Leave more space between your vehicle and others when driving faster.

questions.question: You should signal while turning because it:

options.text: Is required by law to keep your signal on until the turn is complete.
Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
Is always unsafe to turn off your signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, cyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do next.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving at the same speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, let the other vehicle pass safely. Do not speed up or brake suddenly. Stay at a constant speed and allow the vehicle to merge back into your lane.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes means:

options.text: Both lanes go in the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.
Passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates lanes going in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you need to swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is when anything takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is a leading cause of accidents. Any distraction makes you miss important sights and sounds that help you avoid crashes.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Take extra care when backing up.

questions.question: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights on, you should:

options.text: Ask the emergency workers if they need help.
Speed up to pass the incident quickly.
Move to the farthest lane away or slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the farthest lane away or slow down.
questions.explanation: If you see a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights on, move to an available lane away from it. If you cannot move over, slow down to a safe speed and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water sits on the road. Most tires can push water away at speeds up to 35 mph. At speeds above 35 mph, tires cannot move the water away well enough and may lose contact with the road, like water skis.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front of you moves to the right.
When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
When the yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can return to your lane when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The vehicle is being pulled by an animal.
The vehicle is traveling at 25 mph or slower.
The vehicle makes sudden stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is traveling at 25 mph or slower.
questions.explanation: This sign warns other drivers that the vehicle is traveling at 25 mph or slower. You may see it on bicycles, horse-drawn vehicles, or farm equipment.

questions.question: If you parallel park facing downhill, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. This helps stop the car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it frustrates other drivers and causes them to make risky passes. Drive with the flow of traffic at or below the speed limit.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Side mirrors eliminate blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed steady to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery surfaces like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach in the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal early to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb when turning right.

questions.question: When is it legal to drive faster than the posted speed limit?

options.text: Never.
If you think it is safe.
If you are passing another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive faster than the posted speed limit. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but never faster.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming. Be prepared to yield or stop if necessary.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A flagger is ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flagger is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange is used for work zones. When you see orange signs, cones, or barrels, stay alert and prepare for changing driving conditions. This sign warns you that a flagger is coming. You must follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection with a flashing red light. You should:

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is changing direction or narrowing.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is changing direction or narrowing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is turning or getting narrower. You may see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: If you want to enter the freeway but you don't see a gap in traffic, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp if you don't see a space to enter traffic safely. Do not wait at the end of the ramp. You need time and distance to speed up before entering the freeway.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass. When one line is solid and one is broken, only the car on the broken line side can pass. When both lines are solid, no one can pass in either direction.
